summary: self-certificates ships steganographic PEM loader that fetches and executes remote Python
details: index.js loads test/key.pem, strips the RSA PRIVATE KEY headers, base64-decodes the body, and eval()s the result inside generateCertificates(). The decoded JavaScript contains a base64-encoded URL that decodes to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches that endpoint, and pipes the response body into a detached, windowsHide python3/python interpreter via stdin. Any consumer invoking the advertised certificate-generation API triggers execution of attacker-supplied Python on the host. The payload is disguised as an RSA private key and the C2 URL is double base64-encoded to evade static inspection; a certificate library has no legitimate reason to eval PEM contents or spawn a hidden Python interpreter against a remote endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
